newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade taxi drivers protest, compound chaos.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade taxi drivers protest, compound chaos.

text.p: Hundreds of Belgrade taxi drivers blocked the centre of the capital on Monday protesting at police inaction over killing of one of their colleagues.

Some 1,000 taxi drivers, compounding chaos in the city caused by mass demonstrations, parked their vehicles in front of the Federal Parliament building bringing traffic in the heart of the city to a standstill, witnesses said.
Nikola Zivkovic, a 60-year old taxi driver was shot dead early on Monday morning in Belgrade in his taxi, the Belgrade interior ministry said.
Zivkovic was the second taxi driver to be killed this year in a similar fashion and the fifth over the past few months.
Police investigations have not discovered any clues to the murders which apparently have no connection to the ongoing street protests in Belgrade and other towns across Serbia.
"We are here because of what happened at Branko's bridge. Someone is killing taxi drivers while the police are busy beating up peaceful demonstrators," one told Reuters.
Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic's feared security police attacked peaceful protesters overnight, injuring more than 100 people in the worst political violence seen for years in Belgrade.

The opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition has staged almost three months of rallies to protest against the authorities refusal to acknowledge its victory in the 14 biggest Serbian cities, including Belgrade, in November local elections.
